citation: ghostty src/terminal/search/sliding_window.zig (std.ascii.indexOfIgnoreCase), via docs/observations/libghostty-9f9b8d1d.md section 10; row-to-offset alignment from docs/observations/herdr-0.8.0.md section 17
why: The whole of find's matching, and the one place two answers have to agree with each other. Muster counts the matches and libghostty highlights them, so a matcher that differs by a case rule or an overlap rule puts a counter over a screen contradicting it. The positions matter as much as the count: a hit's row is the offset a pane is scrolled by, so an off-by-one here is a find that lands somewhere near the answer.

cases.name: the bottom row is zero rows from the bottom
cases.why: The whole positioning scheme rests on this. A read's last row is the bottom of the pane, and a pane already at the bottom is offset zero - so a match there must ask for no scroll at all rather than for one row.

cases.name: a row further up is that many rows from the bottom
cases.why: The arithmetic the daemon's relative scroll is driven by. Rows arrive oldest first, so the index has to be counted from the other end, which is exactly the direction it is easy to get backwards.

cases.name: matches come back bottom-most first
cases.why: Ghostty's order, and the find bar borrowed from it draws next as an upward chevron on this basis. In a terminal the interesting match is usually the recent one, so the first result somebody sees should be the one nearest where they are looking.

cases.name: case folds, because the renderer's matcher does
cases.why: libghostty searches with std.ascii.indexOfIgnoreCase and there is no way to ask it for anything else. A case-sensitive count here would report one match over a screen highlighting three.

cases.name: several matches on one row read left to right
cases.why: A row is read left to right whichever direction the pane is being walked in. Reversing them inside a row would make next jump backwards across a line and forwards across the pane.

cases.name: matches do not overlap
cases.why: aa in aaaa is two matches, not three. Overlapping would make the counter climb faster than pressing next walks, so the last result would be reachable only by wrapping round.

cases.name: an empty needle matches nowhere
cases.why: Nothing typed yet is not a search that matched everything. The alternative is a bar reporting one hit per row the instant it opens, before anybody has asked for anything.

cases.name: no match is still a search that happened
cases.why: The row count is the reach, and it is what the bar can say it looked at. Zero hits over two rows and zero hits over a thousand are different answers to show a person.

cases.name: the trailing newline is the end of the last row, not a row after it
cases.why: Every read ends with one. Counting it as an empty bottom row would put every real row one further from the bottom than it is, so every hit would scroll one line short - the kind of off-by-one that reads like the daemon's fault.

cases.name: text with no trailing newline reads the same way
cases.why: A backend need not end its answer with one, and the positions may not depend on whether it did.

cases.name: an empty answer is no rows rather than one empty one
cases.why: A pane that has printed nothing. One empty row would report a reach of one and a bottom to scroll to that is not there.

cases.name: blank rows in the middle are still rows
cases.why: A terminal is full of them, and they carry the count that positions everything below. Skipping them would shorten every offset above the first blank line.

cases.name: folding is ASCII only, so STRASSE does not find straße
cases.why: libghostty folds ASCII and nothing else. Full Unicode folding here would find matches the highlight underneath cannot, which is the disagreement this corpus exists to prevent.

cases.name: a non-ASCII needle matches itself
cases.why: Folding ASCII must not mean mangling anything else. Agents print accents, box drawing and emoji constantly, and a needle pasted from the screen has to find what it was copied from.

cases.name: offsets are in bytes, and land on character boundaries
cases.why: The range is stated in bytes because nothing here paints. It still has to be sliceable: 你好 is three bytes a character, so a match after one must start at 3 and not at 1.

cases.name: a needle longer than the row matches nothing rather than panicking
cases.why: Somebody pastes a paragraph into the field. The scan indexes the row by the needle's length, so this is the shape that would read past the end.

cases.name: truncated is carried through, not worked out
cases.why: Only whoever asked knows whether there was more history. Two rows may be all a pane has or the last two of ten thousand, and the bar says so only when it is true.
